correctness.rationale: For every signed one-real-digit/imaginary-repdigit input, exact signed base-B digits give S_B(z)=a^2-mt^2+2ati. The imaginary equality with t!=0 forces 2a=R_m(B); no integer a exists for m=1, and for m>=3 the repdigit R_m(B)>=B^2+B+1>2(B-1)>=2a. At m=2 the real and imaginary equations are equivalent to a=(B+1)/2 and B^2-8t^2=1. The digit inequalities are checked for all Pell solutions. A strict integer descent using (B,t)->(3B-8t,3t-B) verifies the full positive Pell parametrization, including t=1 boundary, while signed t supplies conjugate pairs. B_n=cosh(n log(3+sqrt8)) gives the exact base count. The standalone checker implements the signed digit map and independently verifies a finite exhaustive domain and twelve Pell solutions; no finite experiment substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The full open arXiv:2101.00560v1 specifies the same map and lists the first example 2+4i at base 3, but its Theorem 6 covers only bases 2 through 10, and its all-odd-base Theorem 7 produces real rather than nonreal fixed points. Known Pell parametrization and published unrelated digit-extraction results do not entail fixed points of this map. Targeted published-literature and result-record searches for the complete signed-repdigit pattern and Pell base spectrum yielded no stronger covering implication. The 2022 publisher version and search completeness remain explicit residual risks.
residual_risks: The complete 2022 journal text of the originating paper was not accessible; the preprint was read in full and the journal abstract was checked, but uninspected additions could conceivably touch the claim.
The survey chapter was available only at abstract level; it cannot be used as proof of absence of related results.
Published-mathematics search indexing is incomplete, and absence of returned equivalent statements does not prove universal novelty.
The Pell/square-triangular parametrization is classical; novelty is restricted to the map-specific complete repdigit classification and its nonreal fixed-point base spectrum.

value.rationale: The classification closes a natural entire digit-structured family: any signed imaginary repdigit of arbitrary length and a one-digit real component, directly motivated by the B=3 fixed point listed in the source. The sharp statement that all lengths except two are impossible is structural, not a chosen numerical cutoff. It furnishes infinitely many previously untabulated nonreal fixed points in bases 17, 99, 577, etc. and an exact sparse base spectrum; these are meaningful uniform dynamics questions absent from finite fixed-base censuses. The Pell equation by itself is textbook material, but linking it by a necessary-and-sufficient digit-map theorem to the full natural repdigit class is not merely a renamed Pell sequence. No general all-fixed-points classification is claimed.
